skill.name: docx-official
skill.description: Guides creation, editing, analysis, validation, and redlining of DOCX files using docx-js, OOXML, and bundled Python helpers.
skill.summary: Create, inspect, edit, validate, and redline DOCX files with OOXML-focused workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by OOXML namespace URIs, XML schema imports, Markdown backticks, and long single-line XML templates. The only confirmed issue is dependency guidance that recommends sudo apt-get commands in SKILL.md, which can modify the host if executed automatically. The reviewed scripts use fixed subprocess argument arrays and safe archive extraction patterns; no prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Dependency instructions recommend sudo apt-get installation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before privileged installs and document non-privileged or preinstalled dependency alternatives.

remediation.issue: Large single-line OOXML templates and bundled schema URLs create noisy security alerts.
remediation.suggestion: Add comments that identify these files as inert Office XML templates and standard schemas for future reviewers.

remediation.issue: External tools such as pandoc, LibreOffice, Poppler, git, npm, and Python scripts are part of normal workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command execution user-visible, use fixed arguments, and avoid running generated commands without user confirmation.

content.value_statement: DOCX work requires correct ZIP, XML, and tracked-change handling. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code document workflows and helper scripts.
actual_capabilities: Choose workflows for reading, creating, editing, validating, and redlining DOCX files.
Create new Word documents with docx-js patterns for text, tables, links, images, and page setup.
Unpack and repack Office document ZIP packages with bundled Python helper scripts.
Use a Python Document library to add comments, replies, tracked changes, and relationship metadata.
Validate DOCX and PPTX XML structure with bundled OOXML schemas and relationship checks.
Convert DOCX content to markdown, PDF, or page images when required tools are installed.
limitations: It requires external tools such as pandoc, LibreOffice, Poppler, npm packages, or Python libraries for some workflows.
It works on local files and should be used only with documents the user is allowed to process.
It can guide legal or business document edits, but it does not replace expert review.
OOXML validation can reduce corrupt files, but Microsoft Word behavior still needs final manual verification.

use_cases.title: Draft New Word Documents
use_cases.description: Create structured DOCX files with headings, tables, links, images, lists, headers, and footers.

use_cases.title: Review Contracts with Redlines
use_cases.description: Apply precise tracked changes and comments while preserving existing review markup.

use_cases.title: Repair Document XML
use_cases.description: Unpack, inspect, edit, validate, and repack OOXML files when Word documents need technical fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Document Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to read a DOCX file and recommend the safest text extraction workflow. Explain which tool to use and what output to expect.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Styled DOCX
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a DOCX outline with a title, headings, a table, a bullet list, and a footer. Follow the docx-js formatting rules.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tracked Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan tracked changes for an existing DOCX. Group edits into batches and preserve unchanged text outside insertion and deletion markup.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Complex OOXML Edits
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to unpack a DOCX, inspect relationships and content types, modify document XML, validate the package, and repack the final file.

output_examples.input: Create a DOCX report with sections, a table, and page numbers.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects the docx-js workflow, applies Word-compatible styles, builds real lists, adds tables, and exports a DOCX file.

output_examples.input: Review this contract and show proposed edits as tracked changes.
output: Convert the document to markdown for planning.
Unpack the DOCX package for XML edits.
Apply precise insertions, deletions, and comments in small validated batches.

output_examples.input: Fix a corrupt DOCX after manual XML edits.
output_examples.output: The assistant inspects relationships, content types, schemas, and tracked-change structure before repacking and validating the document.

best_practices: Work on a copied or unpacked document directory before saving changes back to the final file.
Validate each batch of XML edits before moving to the next set of document changes.
Use tracked changes and comments for review documents instead of overwriting disputed text directly.
anti_patterns: Do not run privileged dependency installation commands without explicit user approval.
Do not edit another author's tracked changes by changing their text directly.
Do not skip final validation and manual opening in Word for important documents.

faq.question: Does this skill edit DOCX files directly?
faq.answer: It provides workflows and helper scripts. The assistant still needs access to the user document and permission to edit files.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create new Word documents?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes docx-js guidance for creating Word documents with styles, lists, tables, links, images, and page layout.

faq.question: Can it preserve tracked changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a redlining workflow and Python helpers for comments, insertions, deletions, and validation.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Most document operations are local. Installing missing dependencies may require package repositories or npm access.

faq.question: Is it a substitute for legal review?
faq.answer: No. It can help prepare and validate document edits, but legal, business, and compliance decisions need expert review.
